note.question: When should a service platform expand capacity by financing provider-owned assets, employing providers with platform-owned assets, or renting assets to independent providers?
note.overview: The platform commits to an asset-provision mechanism and investment terms while prospective providers choose whether and how to participate; a competitive bank may finance investment, and the platform later sets price and compensation anticipating provider supply. The paper explicitly solves symmetric pure-strategy equilibria by backward induction.

components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Pareto-selected symmetric pure-strategy equilibrium solved by backward induction. The paper solves operating price, wage and provider supply first, then anticipates these continuation outcomes in the platform's investment and mechanism choice. It restricts attention to symmetric pure-strategy equilibria and selects the Pareto-dominating outcome when multiple equilibria arise.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: In the investment stage, the platform selects an asset-provision mechanism, expansion quantity and long-term terms; prospective providers choose the platform program or bank financing, and the competitive bank decides whether to lend at a break-even rate. In the operating stage, the platform first sets customer price and provider wage. Each new provider's outside option is revealed only after the wage is set; providers then choose platform work or the outside option, productivity is realized, and any loan repayment or default occurs. Long-term employment commits the platform and providers more strongly than short-term rental or provider-owned financing.
